papers.title_in_file: Hybrid Heuristic Algorithms for Adiabatic Quantum Machine Learning Models
papers.what_it_is: A paper proposing r-flip local search with pruning theorems for QUBO and testing a tabu search hybrid against MST2 on large instances.

existing.certainty_reason: Section 4, p.12 states the comparison setup

existing.note: The abstract says this; the body shows it only partly: Algorithm 5 matched more best solutions than MST2 (26 and 25 of 27 for 1-flip at 60 and 600 seconds, against 5 and 10 for MST2), but 2-flip matched fewer than 1-flip.

assertions.value: The authors state that the machine learning models they list, among them linear regression, support vector machines, decision tree splitting, Restricted Boltzmann Machines and Deep Belief Networks, can be converted into a QUBO model, citing other work.
quotes: decision tree splitting (Yawata et al., 2022), Restricted Boltzmann Machines (Xu & Oates, 2021), and Deep Belief Networks (Date et al., 2021), can be converted into a QUBO model.

assertions.value: The authors state that existing quantum annealing solvers face scalability challenges with large QUBO problems, partly due to the Python wrapper implementations.
quotes: existing quantum annealing solvers face scalability challenges with large QUBO problems, partly due to the Python wrapper implementations

assertions.value: The authors state that the candidate-set size experiment used only the larger-scale instances from the literature, up to 38 instances with 2500 to 6000 variables.

assertions.value: The authors state that Algorithms 3, 4 and 5 with r equal to 2 were compared on very large-scale QUBO instances, and the best of them was then compared with the MST2 algorithm that underlies the D-Wave tabu solver.
quotes: Algorithms 3, 4, and 5 (with r = 2) were compared using very large-scale QUBO instances.
the best of these was then compared to a leading algorithm for xᵀQx, the D-Wave tabu solver
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 4, p.12 states the comparison design

assertions.value: The authors state that MST2 was run with default parameters, where the initial tabu search uses 25,000 times the problem size iterations and later starts use 10,000 times the problem size.
quotes: MST2 reported the best results and was chosen with default parameters.
In MST2, the initial tabu search subroutine uses 25,000 * size_of_problem iterations, then reduces to 10,000 * size_of_problem for subsequent starts.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 4, p.12 states the MST2 configuration

assertions.value: The authors state that all algorithms ran on a single core of an Intel Xeon Quad-core E5420 with 8 GB RAM at 2.5 GHz, using GNU C++ compiler version 4.8.5, submitted through Open PBS.
quotes: All algorithms ran on a single core of an Intel Xeon Quad-core E5420 (8 GB RAM, 2.5 GHz) using GNU C++ compiler v4.8.5, submitted via Open PBS

assertions.value: The authors report that in preliminary tests Algorithms 3, 4 and 5 performed well on instances with fewer than 3,000 variables and low density, finding best-known solutions within 10 seconds.
quotes: Preliminary findings showed Algorithms 3, 4, and 5 performed well on instances < 3,000 variables and low density, finding best-known solutions within 10 seconds.
assertions.reader_inference: No table of these preliminary results is in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that very large QUBO instances with 30,000 variables and high density were generated, and that a 600-second CPU limit and r equal to 2 were used for the three algorithms on them.
quotes: Additionally, very-large-scale QUBOs (30,000 variables, high density) were generated.
A 600-second limit for CPU time and r = 2 was used for these three algorithms on these large instances (Table 2).

assertions.value: The authors report that on the very large instances over 10 runs, Algorithm 5 with r equal to 2 was better than Algorithms 3 and 4, and so Algorithm 5 was compared with MST2 at 60- and 600-second CPU limits, 10 runs per instance, with tabu tenure 100.
assertions.anchor: Section 4, p.13 (Table 2 not in the text layer)
quotes: Algorithm 5 (with r=2) was better than Algorithms 3 and 4.
Thus, Algorithm 5 (r = 1 and 2) was compared to MST2, with 60- and 600-second CPU limits per run (10 runs/instance)
A tabu tenure (100) was used for 1- and 2-flip in Algorithm 5 and MST2.

assertions.value: The authors state that the CPU time limit for Algorithm 5 was checked before starting a tabu search, which they consider fair because neither MST2 nor Algorithm 5 is a single-point based method.
quotes: The stopping criterion for Algorithm 5 (CPU time limit) was checked before starting tabu search, considered fair as neither MST2 nor Algorithm 5 is a single-point based method.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 4, p.13 states the stopping rule

assertions.value: The authors report that MST2 showed consistent performance, frequently reaching the same objective function value, while Algorithm 5 starting randomly explores more diversely in short times.
assertions.anchor: Section 4, p.13 (Table 3 not in the text layer)
quotes: MST2 showed consistent performance, frequently reaching the same objective function value.
Algorithm 5, starting randomly, explores more diversely in short times.

assertions.value: The authors report that at the 60-second CPU limit, MST2 matched 5 of 27 best solutions, Algorithm 5 with 1-flip matched 26 of 27 and Algorithm 5 with 2-flip matched 18 of 27, and that MST2 exceeded the 60-second limit for initial solution finding in two large instances.
quotes: In Table 4 (60s): MST2 matched 5/27 best solutions. Algorithm 5 (1-flip) matched 26/27; Algorithm 5 (2-flip) matched 18/27.
MST2 exceeded the 60s limit for initial solution finding in two large instances.
assertions.reader_inference: The text does not say how 'best' is defined (best known or best among the three).

assertions.value: The authors report that at the 600-second CPU limit, MST2 matched 10 of 27 best solutions, Algorithm 5 with 1-flip matched 25 of 27 and Algorithm 5 with 2-flip matched 23 of 27.
quotes: In Table 5 (600s), MST2 matched 10/27 best solutions. Algorithm 5 (1-flip) matched 25/27; Algorithm 5 (2-flip) matched 23/27.

assertions.value: The authors state that the one-flip strategy showed better overall performance at both the 60 and 600-second limits.
quotes: The 1-flip strategy showed better overall performance at both 60 and 600-second limits.
assertions.reader_inference: This sits uneasily with the abstract's emphasis on the r-flip strategy, since r equal to 1 is plain tabu search with 1-flip local search.

assertions.value: The authors report that MST2 has less variation in time when it reaches the same objective function value, while Algorithm 5 with r-flip has a wider range of computing times.
quotes: MST2 has less variation when it reaches the same objective function value.
Algorithm 5 (r-flip) has a wider range of computing times.

assertions.value: The authors state that, compared to MST2, the r-flip strategy produces high-quality solutions faster and is easily implemented as a warm start local search for many quantum annealing solvers.
quotes: the r-flip strategy produces high-quality solutions faster and is easily implemented as a
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against the original MST2 C++ code on a CPU, not a quantum annealer or the D-Wave wrapper; the warm-start use was not tested in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report a Friedman test over MST2 and the two tabu search variants on 27 complete experimental instances with chi-squared statistic 19.9808 and p-value 4.5839e-05.
quotes: This comparison was based on 27 complete experimental instances
The Friedman chi-squared statistic calculated was 19.9808.
The associated p-value for this test was extremely small, 4.5839e-05

assertions.value: The authors report Nemenyi post-hoc p-values of 0.000176 for MST2 against 1-flip, 0.001172 for MST2 against 2-flip, and 0.882488 for 1-flip against 2-flip.
quotes: For the pair MST2 versus 1-flip, the p-value was 0.000176.
for MST2 versus 2-flip, the p-value was 0.001172
test yielded a p-value of 0.882488

assertions.value: The authors report Bonferroni-corrected pairwise Wilcoxon p-values of 0.000050 for MST2 against 1-flip, 0.000011 for MST2 against 2-flip, and 1.000000 for 1-flip against 2-flip.
quotes: The comparison between MST2 and 1-flip yielded a p-value of 0.000050
MST2 and 2-flip produced an even smaller p-value of 0.000011
the p-value after Bonferroni correction was 1.000000
assertions.reader_inference: The paper concludes that 1-flip and 2-flip outperform MST2 'assuming MST2 had higher DT values'; the direction rests on that assumption, since the tests give only that the groups differ.

assertions.value: The authors state that the cost of r-flips still grows with r despite pruning by Theorem 1 and Proposition 1, and that performance is sensitive to parameter tuning, including the r-value, tabu tenure and the M-value threshold.
quotes: The computational cost of r-flips, though reduced by theoretical pruning (Theorem 1, Proposition 1), still grows with r
Performance is also sensitive to parameter tuning, including the r-value, tabu tenure, the M-value threshold

assertions.value: The authors state that algorithm efficacy can vary with QUBO instance characteristics (size, density, coefficient distribution), and that success depends on achieving a good 1-flip optimum before applying r-flip pruning.
quotes: algorithm efficacy can vary with QUBO instance characteristics (size, density, coefficient distribution)
such as achieving a good 1-flip optimum before applying r-flip pruning strategies.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that the r-flip strategy can solve very-large-scale QUBO instances in 600 seconds and uses significantly less time than MST2 to find best-known solutions on the benchmark problems.
quotes: Computational results demonstrate a significantly smaller number of candidates for r-flip implementations.

the novel r-flip strategy is capable of solving very-large-scale QUBO instances in 600 seconds, using significantly less time to find the best-known solutions for the benchmark problems compared to MST2
assertions.reader_inference: The reported tables show matches of best solutions per time limit, not time-to-best; and 1-flip beat 2-flip.
